newsitem.title: USA: Dow claws back ground at midday, techs lower.
newsitem.headline: Dow claws back ground at midday, techs lower.

text.p: U.S. blue-chip stocks were climbing higher by midday on Thursday, as the release of more solid corporate earnings reports put a lid on early profit-taking that followed the previous session's rally.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which pushed past the 8,000-point milestone Wednesday, moved out of negative territory to trade up around 19 points at 8058.
The Nasdaq composite, whose technology stocks have led the index higher in recent days, also climbed off its session lows. It was down around four points, or 0.27 percent, at 1576.

"It seems impossible to hold this market back," Sam Stovall, an analyst at Standard & Poor's Industry reports, said. "In general, investors are very opmistic about the outlook for interest rates and the outlook for earnings."
A rise in stocks coincided with gains by the long bond, which firmed 10/32 to yield 6.46 percent.
The Dow was bolstered by slightly better-than-forecast results from component Merck and Co Inc.
Shares of the U.S. drug maker jumped 7-1/4 to 105-3/4 after reporting second-quarter earnings of $0.96 per share, 20 percent more than it earned in the year-ago second quarter.

McDonald's Corp, another Dow component, also gained after it posted second-quarter earnings of $0.63 per share versus $0.59 in the year-ago quarter. The restaurant chain's stock rose 14/16 at 50-15/16.
Shares of Sears, Roebuck and Co rose 2-3/8 to 58-7/8 after it reported second-quarter operating earnings of $0.78 versus $0.67 in last year's second quarter.
"Earnings, by and large, have been good," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp, said.
Plus, the outlook for the U.S. economy could not be rosier, analysts said.

"We are nervous about valuations, but given the continued outlook for low inflation, moderate growth and prospects for lower interest rates, the stock market has just mushroomed here," said Harvey Hirshhorn, Stein Roe and Farnham chief economist and investment strategist.
Technology stocks did not fare as well as blue-chip companies in Thursday's market, pausing after recent surges.
"These companies have had a huge run so they are entitled to pull back here," Stein said. "Groups are playing catch-up. It's rotational."
The high-tech sector, lifted yesterday by above-forecast results from chipmaker Intel Corp, was awaiting fourth-quarter results from Microsoft Corp due later.
The First Call consensus earnings estimate was $0.79 per share compared with $0.44 in the year-ago quarter.
The stock, which drifted down earlier in the session after soaring on Wednesday, was up 1-3/16 at 149-5/8.
Shares of Woolworth Corp gained two to 37-1/16. The company announced plans to close more than 400 five-and-10 cent stores in the United States.
Lucent Technologies Inc said it would acquire Octel Communications Corp for $1.8 billion, beefing up its voice mail, facsimile and messaging technology business.
Lucent's stock shed two points to 86-1/2 while Octel rose 3-11/16 to 30-7/16.

Aspect Telecommunications Corp stock lost six points to 20-1/4. The company reported second-quarter earnings of $0.24 per primary share compared with $0.18 a year ago. Goldman Sachs said it lowered its rating on the stock to market perform from market outperform.
((Wall Street desk 212-859-1730))
